name: Distracted Boyfriend
scene: A man walking with his girlfriend turns to ogle another woman passing by. Three labels: the original loyalty/girlfriend (slot 0), the new shiny distraction (slot 1), the man being tempted (slot 2).
when: User is abandoning something sensible they have for a shinier new obsession. Pattern: existing thing → new shiny thing → the user/themself.

example.user_said: I'm rewriting our working Node auth in Rust because I'm bored.

name: Drake Hotline Bling
scene: Two stacked panels of Drake. Top: recoiling with hand up — rejection. Bottom: smiling and pointing — approval.
when: Comparing two options where one is rejected and one is preferred. Slot 0 (top) = rejected option, slot 1 (bottom) = chosen option.

example.user_said: I read the docs once then immediately started guessing.

name: This Is Fine
scene: A cartoon dog sitting in a burning room sipping coffee. Slot 0 (top) sets up the disaster, slot 1 (bottom) is usually 'this is fine' or a variant of the user's denial.
when: User describes an obvious disaster but talks about it like it's normal. The contrast IS the joke.

example.user_said: Prod crashes every hour but nobody is paged so we're good.

name: X, X Everywhere
scene: Buzz Lightyear gestures broadly while telling Woody '[X], [X] everywhere'. Slot 0 is the noun alone, slot 1 is '[noun] everywhere'.
when: User keeps repeating the same theme/topic — call it out by saying it's everywhere.

example.user_said: Everyone at this conference will not shut up about agents.

name: Afraid to Ask Andy
scene: Andy from Parks & Rec, hands on cheeks, nervous. Slot 0 = an awkward admission of long-running ignorance, slot 1 = the absurd lengths to avoid asking.
when: User pretends to know a term/concept they have actually been faking for ages. Self-deprecating energy.

example.user_said: I've used Kubernetes for years, totally know what a sidecar is.
captions: still no idea what a sidecar is

name: Success Kid
scene: A baby with a clenched fist of victory in front of a beach. Tiny, petty wins celebrated like championships.
when: User celebrates a trivial accomplishment with disproportionate enthusiasm. Slot 0 = setup, slot 1 = the petty victory.

example.user_said: I remembered to put pants on before joining standup today.

name: Insanity Wolf
scene: Black-and-white snarling wolf in front of moon. Slot 0 = a normal-ish setup line, slot 1 = an unhinged escalation.
when: Take something the user said is mildly off and escalate it to a deranged extreme.

example.user_said: I sometimes skip the unit tests when I'm in a hurry.

name: Daily Struggle / Two Buttons
scene: A sweating man in a red shirt stares at two red buttons, panicking. Each caption labels one button — usually two options that are basically the same or both bad.
when: User agonizes over a false choice between two options that do not actually differ.

example.user_said: Should I quit or just keep complaining on Twitter forever?

name: It's a Trap
scene: Admiral Ackbar mid-yell. Single caption: a restatement of an obvious trap as a warning.
when: User describes a transparent trap with zero awareness. Restate the trap so it sounds like the warning the user should have heard.

example.user_said: My boss said it'd be a quick 30-minute call to discuss feedback.

name: Philosoraptor
scene: A velociraptor in The Thinker pose. Two-panel fake-deep question. Slot 0 = pseudo-philosophical setup, slot 1 = ironic punchline that reveals the question is silly.
when: User asks a fake-deep or oddly profound-sounding question about something mundane.

example.user_said: If I name my variable better, does that make me a better person?
captions: if I name the variable better
do I become a better person
